trials.name: EVITA
trials.full_name: Evaluation of Intravenous Therapies for Asthma
trials.question: What is the clinical and cost-effectiveness of IV bronchodilators in children with severe acute asthma unresponsive to maximal inhaled therapy?
trials.design: Phase 3 open-label 3-arm RCT · Research without prior consent (deferred consent)
trials.population: Children and young people aged 2–18 years
inclusion: Age 2–18 years (up to the day before 19th birthday)
Known asthma or acute wheeze considered asthma by the assessing clinician
Unresponsive to maximal inhaled bronchodilator therapy (usually 3 back-to-back high-dose salbutamol + ipratropium), OR critical asthma requiring immediate IV treatment
trials.exclusion_brief: Immediate need for invasive ventilation · Co-existing chronic lung disease · Severe renal or liver disease · Known IV bronchodilator contraindication · Previous EVITA randomisation · Beta-blocker or regular theophylline use · Another CTIMP in last 3 months
arms: IV salbutamol — 15 micrograms/kg (max 250 micrograms) over 5–10 min, then 1 microgram/kg/min (max 20 micrograms/min)
IV magnesium sulfate — 40 mg/kg (max 2 g) over 20 min
IV aminophylline — 5 mg/kg (max 500 mg) over 20 min, then 1 mg/kg/hr (age 2–11) or 0.5 mg/kg/hr (age ≥12)
trials.primary_outcome: Asthma severity score 2 hours after randomisation
trials.consent: Deferred consent for trial intervention. Prospective consent for process evaluation, health economics, and questionnaire.
trials.what_to_do: Register eligible patient on the trial database — this randomises them to one of the three IV arms. Research nurse will collect further trial data. Use local prescribing practice for preparation and administration.
